benchmarks.name: CrossMed (MAT compositional generalization, classification)
benchmarks.description: CrossMed (arXiv 2511.11034, IIT Delhi): compositional-generalization benchmark for medical MLLMs using Modality-Anatomy-Task (MAT) triplets; reformulates CheXpert, SIIM-ACR, BraTS 2020, MosMedData into 20,200 multiple-choice VQA instances; Related / Unrelated / zero-overlap splits; classification accuracy and segmentation cIoU. Models are fine-tuned on splits (LLaVA-Vicuna-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B), so no off-the-shelf model scores.

benchmarks.name: MMR-Bench (multimodal LLM routing)
benchmarks.description: MMR-Bench (arXiv 2601.17814): offline benchmark for cost-aware routing among 10 candidate MLLMs (GPT-5 series, Gemini 2.5, Claude, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL) over 8 datasets in 3 scenarios (OCR, general VQA, math reasoning), 11,000 instances with precomputed per-instance utility + normalized cost; metrics nAUC, peak score Ps, quality-neutral cost QNC. Results are router methods, not models.

benchmarks.name: MultAttrEval (multimodal long-document attribution)
benchmarks.description: MultAttrEval (arXiv 2607.01420, UMass + Adobe): 698 question-answer-attribution (QAA) triplets over 20 long image-dense documents (5 domains) in text-only (176), image-only (255) and multimodal (267) regimes, with fine-grained ground-truth attributions; 90 probe QAAs; attribution precision/recall/F1. Paper results compare attribution pipelines (Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B / GPT-5.4 prompting vs MultAttnAttrib).

benchmarks.name: LanEvil++ (lane detection / ADVLM robustness to environmental illusions)
benchmarks.metric: accuracy / F1 (LD); GPT score / language score (ADVLM)
benchmarks.description: LanEvil++ (arXiv 2607.05783): CARLA-built robustness benchmark of 14 environmental illusion types (road damage, traffic obstruction, shadow, reflection) over 94 editable 3D scenes: 90,292 annotated images, 1,596 video clips, 41,855 QA pairs; evaluates lane-detection models (accuracy/F1) and autonomous-driving VLMs (GPT score, language score; perturbed vs original gap). Evaluated ADVLMs are DriveLM, Dolphins, OmniDrive (research models, not in DB).

benchmarks.name: SafeManip (temporal safety in robotic manipulation)
benchmarks.metric: per-trigger violation rate / exposure rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: SafeManip (arXiv 2605.12386, 2026): property-driven benchmark evaluating temporal safety of robot foundation-model policies from low-level rollouts; 8 physical+semantic safety categories; LTLf temporal properties grounded from manipulation predicates; ManipVerse property ontology; 20 enforced specifications; per-trigger metrics (violations per triggered event, exposure % of rollout); instantiated on RoboCasa365 and LIBERO auditing 7 policies (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.5/N1.6, RLDX-1, Cosmos Policy, OpenVLA).

benchmarks.name: CyberMaskQA-250 MCQA (average accuracy)
benchmarks.description: CyberMaskQA (arXiv 2605.24765, UCSD, May 2026): privacy-aware operational cybersecurity QA benchmark; CyberMaskQA-250 = 250 human-validated multiple-choice questions grounded in organizational context (asset roles, privileges, logs) across categories Identity & Access Mgmt, Security Posture & Prevention, Threat Detection & Incident Analysis, Incident Response & Escalation; expanded to 2,000 items; also a PII/operational-entity masking task scored by precision/recall. One-shot prompting, letter-only answers.

benchmarks.name: Pluralis v0.1 (multicultural multimodal multilingual AI risk & reliability)
benchmarks.description: Pluralis v0.1 (arXiv 2607.06196, Jul 2026): culture-first multimodal safety dataset of 6,448 text+image prompts natively sourced in six Asia-Pacific locales (Bangladesh, India, Korea, Pakistan, Singapore, Taiwan) and eight languages; innocuous text + image pairs that jointly trigger locale-specific legal/cultural violations; separates universal safety hazards from locale-conditioned cultural appropriateness; scored by Judge-Pluralis agreement-gated LLM-judge ensemble. Paper reports only anonymized SUTs.

benchmarks.description: AgentFootprint (PolyU, arXiv 2607.11149, Jul 2026): first cross-framework benchmark of the bytes an LLM agent run leaves on disk (logs, checkpoints, debug traces). Metric suite: total retention S_total, channel composition, duplication D, growth exponent alpha, zstd compressibility, conversation-history reconstructability R (0-3). 8 frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, SmolAgents, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex, Agno, InfiAgent) over 1,061 sandboxed runs; file-QA suite 10 tasks x 3 reps. Framework-level (harness) results, no model leaderboard. status dataset-only.

benchmarks.name: MKG-RAG-Bench (multimodal KG-augmented generation retrieval)
benchmarks.description: MKG-RAG-Bench (Penn State, KDD'26, arXiv 2606.26458): retrieval benchmark for multimodal-knowledge-graph RAG with two splits — MKG-RAG-Bench-G (general; 48,908/6,113/6,115 train/val/test queries, 25,517 triplets, ~30% multimodal) and MKG-RAG-Bench-M (medical; 4,781/597/599 queries, 18,468 triplets, ~43% multimodal). Questions synthesized by GPT-5 from masked triplets; metrics retrieval Recall/MRR and generation EM/F1/Contains@1/BLEU at K=5. Paper compares retriever families, not LLMs. https://github.com/XiaochenWang-PSU/MKG-RAG-Bench. status dataset-only.

benchmarks.name: Blueprint-Bench v1 (Andon Labs)
benchmarks.description: Blueprint-Bench v1 (Andon Labs, arXiv 2509.25229, Sep 2025): spatial-intelligence benchmark — turn ~20 interior photos of an apartment into a 2D floor plan; 50 apartments; scoring = similarity of room-connectivity graph and room size ranking vs ground truth (edge overlap 50%, degree correlation 20%, density 10%, room count 10%, door count 5%, ...), compared with a random baseline and humans. Evaluated LLMs (GPT-5, Claude 4 Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-4, GPT-5-mini), image models (GPT-Image, NanoBanana) and agents (Codex CLI, Claude Code); most models at or below random baseline. Results in figures only. Generation code https://github.com/AndonLabs/Blueprint-Bench-generation. Successor: blueprint_bench_2. status dataset-only.

benchmarks.name: DeliberationBench (LLM influence vs Deliberative Polls)
benchmarks.metric: association of LLM-induced opinion shift with deliberative-poll shift
benchmarks.description: DeliberationBench (arXiv 2603.10018, IASEAI'26): normative benchmark for LLM persuasive influence using Deliberative Polling as reference; preregistered RCT with 4,088 U.S. participants discussing 65 policy proposals (America in One Room + Meta Community Forum polls) with six LLMs (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4, Grok 4, Llama 4 Scout, DeepSeek V3.1). Code/data github.com/insperatum/deliberationbench. Per-model results only in figures.

benchmarks.name: CORTEX (structured reasoning for 3D chest CT)
benchmarks.description: CORTEX (arXiv 2606.27264, MBZUAI/HPI): structured four-stage diagnostic reasoning traces (task understanding, visual observation, diagnostic reasoning, answer synthesis) built on CT-RATE; 76,160 validated traces over open-ended VQA, closed-ended VQA and report generation; traces generated by MedGemma 27B, Qwen-3 32B, Baichuan-M2 32B, Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Flash and judged by GPT-5.4-mini with radiologist review. Dataset + code on GitHub/HuggingFace.

benchmarks.name: MINDGAMES live arena — social and strategic reasoning for multi-agent LLMs
benchmarks.description: MINDGAMES (arXiv:2605.29512): live competition arena over four game environments (Colonel Blotto, Three-Player Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, Codenames, Secret Mafia) with TrueSkill ratings, Efficient vs Unlimited divisions and a frozen reference set (MG-Ref) for offline evaluation of new models.

benchmarks.name: WorldLines Memory QA — Event R@5
benchmarks.description: WorldLines (arXiv:2606.18847): long-horizon stateful embodied-agent memory benchmark; 310 Memory QA samples over multi-day household traces; Event R@5 measures recall of the exact state-changing event among top-5 retrieved evidence (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: WorldLines downstream embodied planning — Plan score
benchmarks.description: WorldLines (arXiv:2606.18847): downstream embodied household planning from retrieved long-term memory; Plan dimension score per memory system (Table 4).

benchmarks.name: Lost in Aggregation — one-shot maze navigation SR (coordinate input, small mazes)
benchmarks.description: Lost in Aggregation (arXiv:2606.22219): multi-scale diagnostic benchmark for LLM grid-maze spatial navigation (Fine/Meso/Macro levels). Module 1 one-shot success rate with coordinate-list input, pooled over maze sizes 3, 5, 7 (n=150 per cell) (Table 3).

benchmarks.name: Lost in Aggregation — one-shot navigation SR at 10x10
benchmarks.description: Lost in Aggregation (arXiv:2606.22219): Module 2 one-shot navigation success rate on 10x10 mazes, where composed navigation collapses while isolated Fine/Macro/MesoxMacro probes stay above chance (Table 4).

benchmarks.name: Lost in Aggregation — coupled MesoxMacro probe accuracy at 10x10
benchmarks.description: Lost in Aggregation (arXiv:2606.22219): Module 2 isolated coupled Meso x Macro multiple-choice probe accuracy at 10x10 (chance 0.25) (Table 4).

benchmarks.name: DynamicMem — habit score on State Completion
benchmarks.description: DynamicMem (arXiv:2606.22877): long-horizon memory benchmark in real-world settings; agents read a growing user trajectory and are probed at checkpoints C1-C5 over habits, preferences and attributes. Habit score under the State Completion (SC) task; five memory systems with gpt-5-mini as the answer-generation LLM, gemini-3-flash-preview construction and gpt-5.4 as judge (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: DynamicMem — habit score on Personalized Service
benchmarks.description: DynamicMem (arXiv:2606.22877): habit score under the Personalized Service (PS) task, which reads the same memory as State Completion but requires proactive routine selection; habits collapse relative to SC (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.description: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE): multimodal closed-ended academic benchmark at the frontier of human knowledge, built by CAIS and Scale AI with thousands of subject-matter experts (Phan et al., 2025). 2,500 expert-written questions (≈14% need an image) across dozens of subjects (math-heavy, plus humanities and natural sciences), multiple-choice and exact-match short-answer formats; each question has an unambiguous, non-searchable answer. Metric: accuracy (%), judged by an LLM answer-equality checker; calibration error also reported. Some boards (e.g. Artificial Analysis) use the 2,158-question text-only subset. arXiv:2501.14249; https://lastexam.ai Default setting: no tools. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14249

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience Index

Metric: Omniscience Index, bounded -100..100 = %correct − %incorrect (hallucinated) answers with abstentions scored 0, so 0 means as many correct as wrong answers. arXiv:2511.13029; https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/omniscience https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13029

Headline score = average of the 10-option standard and vision settings; metric accuracy (%). License Apache-2.0. arXiv:2409.02813; HF MMMU/MMMU_Pro https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02813

benchmarks.name: Cached input price ($/1M tokens)
benchmarks.description: Price metric (not a benchmark): list API price in USD per 1 million input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache (cache-read / 'cached input' tier), first-party or OpenRouter rate at collection time; lower is better. OpenRouter exposes it as pricing.input_cache_read in USD per token (×1e6 = $/1M); OpenAI lists it as the 'Cached input' column. Excludes cache-write surcharges. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models

benchmarks.name: Blended price ($/1M tokens)
benchmarks.description: Price metric (not a benchmark): blended API price in USD per 1 million tokens, a weighted mix of input and output list prices (Artificial Analysis / llm-stats convention: 3 input : 1 output tokens) at collection time; lower is better. Derived from per-token prompt/completion prices such as OpenRouter pricing.prompt / pricing.completion (USD per token). https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models

benchmarks.name: Input cost @ 1M tokens (USD per 1M)
benchmarks.description: Price metric (not a benchmark): USD list price per 1M input tokens in the provider's long-context tier (prompts above the tier threshold, e.g. >200K/272K tokens, which many APIs bill at a higher 'Long context' rate); lower is better. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

benchmarks.name: Output cost @ 1M tokens (USD per 1M)
benchmarks.description: Price metric (not a benchmark): USD list price per 1M output tokens when the request is in the provider's long-context tier (long prompts billed at the 'Long context' rate); lower is better. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

benchmarks.name: CyberGym (vuln-reproduction success rate)

Metric: reproduction success rate (%), also counts newly found zero-days. arXiv:2506.02548; https://cybergym.io https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02548

benchmarks.name: AA Analyst Agent (pass^5)

Each question is run 5 times; headline metric pass^5 = share of questions answered correctly on all 5 attempts (pass@1 and pass@5 also reported). Standalone, not in the Intelligence Index. https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/aa-analyst-agent

benchmarks.name: VideoMMMU

benchmarks.name: Dynamic Emotional Reliance
benchmarks.description: OpenAI Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks with adversarial user simulations (GPT-5.x system cards, 2026): multi-turn conversations that evolve in response to the model's outputs, driven by realistic adversarial simulated users; every assistant turn is checked against policy. Metric not_unsafe = share of assistant messages that do not violate safety policy (0–1, higher is better). Internal set. Domain: emotional reliance (unhealthy emotional dependence on the model). https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5/gpt-5-5.pdf

benchmarks.name: Dynamic Self-harm
benchmarks.description: OpenAI Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks with adversarial user simulations (GPT-5.x system cards, 2026): multi-turn conversations that evolve in response to the model's outputs, driven by realistic adversarial simulated users; every assistant turn is checked against policy. Metric not_unsafe = share of assistant messages that do not violate safety policy (0–1, higher is better). Internal set. Domain: self-harm. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5/gpt-5-5.pdf

benchmarks.name: First-Person Fairness (harm_overall)
benchmarks.description: OpenAI first-person fairness evaluation (system cards, 2025–26): 600+ challenging multi-turn prompts where the user first shares a name statistically associated with males or females (e.g. Brian vs Ashley) and then makes a request; GPT-4o grades harmful stereotype differences between responses. Metric harm_overall = expected rate of biased answer differences between male vs female names; lower is better. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5/gpt-5-5.pdf

benchmarks.name: Cyber Safety Production Data Policy Compliance
benchmarks.description: OpenAI cyber-safety evaluation (GPT-5.x system cards, 2026): held-out chat and agentic (incl. multi-turn) prompts spanning benign, dual-use and disallowed cyber requests (malware deployment, credential theft, exfiltration; MITRE ATT&CK-grounded scenarios), selected to be challenging. Metric policy compliance rate (0–1, higher is better). Split: deidentified production data. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5/gpt-5-5.pdf

benchmarks.name: Cyber Safety Synthetic Data Policy Compliance
benchmarks.description: OpenAI cyber-safety evaluation (GPT-5.x system cards, 2026): held-out chat and agentic (incl. multi-turn) prompts spanning benign, dual-use and disallowed cyber requests (malware deployment, credential theft, exfiltration; MITRE ATT&CK-grounded scenarios), selected to be challenging. Metric policy compliance rate (0–1, higher is better). Split: synthetic data covering rare policy-relevant scenarios. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5/gpt-5-5.pdf

benchmarks.name: Tacit Knowledge Troubleshooting Cons At 32
benchmarks.description: OpenAI biorisk eval 'Tacit knowledge and troubleshooting' (system cards; built with Gryphon Scientific): uncontaminated in-house multiple-choice questions spanning all 5 stages of biothreat creation that require tacit lab knowledge or hands-on troubleshooting experience. Metric: accuracy with consensus@32 (majority answer over 32 samples). https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03267

benchmarks.name: Protocol Troubleshooting
benchmarks.description: OpenAI biorisk eval ProtocolQA Open-Ended (system cards): 108 FutureHouse ProtocolQA multiple-choice questions rewritten as open-ended short answers — each introduces egregious errors into a published wet-lab protocol, describes the observed result and asks how to fix it; compared against 19 PhD wet-lab experts. Metric accuracy (pass@1). https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03267

benchmarks.name: Gray Swan IPI (indirect prompt injection ASR)
benchmarks.description: Gray Swan IPI Arena benchmark (external red-teaming by Gray Swan AI, reported in OpenAI/Google system cards 2025–26): indirect prompt-injection attacks embedded in untrusted content across coding, tool-use and computer-use agent scenarios (data theft/destruction, system compromise, unauthorized transactions); latest set has 1,810 curated attacks. Metric: attack success rate (%) across multiple attempts per scenario; lower is better. resource/openai_gpt-6-astra_system-card_2026-09.pdf

benchmarks.name: Single-turn harmful request — claude.ai harmless rate
benchmarks.description: Anthropic single-turn harmlessness evaluation (Claude system cards): single-turn prompts spanning clearly harmful and clearly benign requests across Usage-Policy areas, run in multiple languages. This id: harmless response rate on clearly harmful requests in the claude.ai configuration (higher is better). resource/anthropic_claude-opus-5.5_system-card_2026-09.pdf

benchmarks.name: Suicide/self-harm — API multi-turn appropriate
benchmarks.description: Anthropic suicide & self-harm multi-turn evaluation (Claude system cards): simulated users (persona/objective specs written by policy experts, user turns generated by a Claude model) hold conversations involving suicide/self-harm risk; metric multi-turn appropriate response rate = share of conversations where the model behaved appropriately throughout (rubric-graded), API without system prompt. resource/anthropic_claude-opus-5.5_system-card_2026-09.pdf

benchmarks.name: Claude Code dual-use & benign success
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Claude Code agentic-safety evaluation (Claude system cards): malicious-use-of-coding-agents test set mixing malicious, dual-use and benign security requests in Claude Code; this id = success/assist rate on dual-use and benign tasks (higher is better, i.e. not over-refusing). resource/anthropic_claude-opus-5.5_system-card_2026-09.pdf

benchmarks.name: Officeqa
benchmarks.description: OfficeQA (Databricks, 2025): grounded enterprise-reasoning benchmark over a large corpus of historical U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents — the agent must locate relevant tables across documents and do precise numerical reasoning; usually run agentically with extracted text and code execution. Metric accuracy (%). https://github.com/databricks/officeqa

benchmarks.name: OfficeQA Pro
benchmarks.description: OfficeQA (Databricks, 2025): grounded enterprise-reasoning benchmark over a large corpus of historical U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents — the agent must locate relevant tables across documents and do precise numerical reasoning; usually run agentically with extracted text and code execution. Metric accuracy (%). OfficeQA Pro: the harder 133-question subset recommended for frontier models. https://github.com/databricks/officeqa

benchmarks.name: Programbench
benchmarks.description: ProgramBench (Yang, Lieret et al., 2026): long-context agentic coding benchmark of 200 program-reconstruction tasks — given only a program's behaviour/documentation the agent must rebuild it from scratch, from compact CLI tools to FFmpeg, SQLite and the PHP interpreter; scored by the share of hidden tests passed (tasks counted solved at ≥95% tests). arXiv:2605.03546 https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03546

benchmarks.name: MTEB English v2
benchmarks.description: MTEB English v2 (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark; Muennighoff et al., HF/Cohere, 2022; v2 English suite from MMTEB, Enevoldsen et al., 2025): text-embedding benchmark; the English v2 suite is a down-sampled, de-duplicated set of 41 English tasks across classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. Metric: mean task score (main metric per task, e.g. nDCG@10 for retrieval, accuracy for classification). arXiv:2210.07316 / 2502.13595; https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard

benchmarks.name: MTEB Multilingual (MMTEB)
benchmarks.description: MMTEB (Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark; Enevoldsen et al., 2025): community-driven expansion of MTEB to 500+ quality-controlled tasks across 250+ languages (plus code, long-document and instruction-following retrieval); the leaderboard 'Multilingual' benchmark is a down-sampled 131-task subset. Metric: mean task score. arXiv:2502.13595 https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13595

benchmarks.name: Ocrbench
benchmarks.description: OCRBench (Liu et al., HUST, 2023): OCR capability benchmark for large multimodal models — 1,000 manually verified question-answer pairs drawn from 29 datasets over five tasks (text recognition, scene-text VQA, document VQA, key information extraction, handwritten math expression recognition). Score = number correct out of 1000 (often shown as %). arXiv:2305.07895 https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07895

benchmarks.name: OCRBench (v1)
benchmarks.description: OCRBench (Liu et al., HUST, 2023): OCR capability benchmark for large multimodal models — 1,000 manually verified question-answer pairs drawn from 29 datasets over five tasks (text recognition, scene-text VQA, document VQA, key information extraction, handwritten math expression recognition). Score = number correct out of 1000 (often shown as %). arXiv:2305.07895 (v1, as distinct from OCRBench v2.) https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07895

benchmarks.name: LongBench v2
benchmarks.description: LongBench v2 (Bai et al., Tsinghua/Zhipu, 2024): 503 challenging multiple-choice questions with contexts from 8K to 2M words across six categories (single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, long in-context learning, long-dialogue history, code-repository and long structured-data understanding), written by ~100 experts; human experts reach 53.7% under 15 min. Metric accuracy (%), also split easy/hard and short/medium/long. arXiv:2412.15204; https://longbench2.github.io https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15204

benchmarks.name: Kmmlu
benchmarks.description: KMMLU (Son et al., HAE-RAE/EleutherAI, 2024): Korean MMLU-style benchmark of 35,030 expert-level four-option multiple-choice questions across 45 subjects (humanities to STEM), sourced from original Korean exams rather than translations. Metric accuracy (%), typically 5-shot. arXiv:2402.11548; HF HAERAE-HUB/KMMLU https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11548

benchmarks.name: Cybench (CTF)
benchmarks.description: Cybench (Zhang et al., Stanford, 2024): framework of 40 professional-level Capture-the-Flag tasks from 4 recent CTF competitions (HackTheBox, SekaiCTF, Glacier, HKCert) spanning crypto, web, reverse engineering, forensics, pwn and misc, with subtasks; agents act in a Kali Linux environment. Metric: unguided success rate (% of tasks whose flag is captured), also subtask-guided performance. arXiv:2408.08926; https://cybench.github.io https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08926

benchmarks.name: OpenBookQA
benchmarks.description: OpenBookQA (Mihaylov et al., AI2, 2018): ~6,000 four-option elementary science questions (500 test) probing application of a 'book' of 1,329 core science facts plus broad common knowledge; human ~92%. Metric accuracy (%). arXiv:1809.02789 https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.02789

benchmarks.name: OmniDocBench v1.6
benchmarks.description: OmniDocBench (Ouyang et al., Shanghai AI Lab/OpenDataLab, 2024): PDF document-parsing benchmark with rich block- and span-level annotations (text, titles, tables, formulas, reading order) over diverse page types (papers, textbooks, financial reports, newspapers, handwritten notes, slides), English and Chinese; v1.6 has 1,651 pages incl. a 296-page hard subset. End-to-end metrics: text Edit distance, formula CDM, table TEDS, reading-order Edit; Overall = ((1−TextEdit)×100 + TableTEDS + FormulaCDM)/3. arXiv:2412.07626; github.com/opendatalab/OmniDocBench This id: v1.6 Overall score (higher is better). https://github.com/opendatalab/OmniDocBench

End-to-end metrics: text Edit distance, formula CDM, table TEDS, reading-order Edit; Overall = ((1−TextEdit)×100 + TableTEDS + FormulaCDM)/3. arXiv:2412.07626; github.com/opendatalab/OmniDocBench This id: overall normalized edit distance on English pages (lower is better; v1.0/1.5 protocol). https://github.com/opendatalab/OmniDocBench

benchmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1 — 50% success
benchmarks.description: METR Time Horizon (Kwa et al., METR, 2025): measures autonomous capability as the length of tasks (in human-expert completion time) that a model completes with a given success probability, fitted by logistic regression of success vs. log human time over software/ML/cyber tasks (RE-Bench, HCAST, SWAA). TH1.1 (Jan 2026) uses 228 tasks and Inspect infrastructure. Unit: minutes (or hours) of human time; higher is better. arXiv:2503.14499; https://metr.org This id: 50% time horizon, TH1.1. https://metr.org/blog/2026-1-29-time-horizon-1-1/

benchmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1 — 80% success
benchmarks.description: METR Time Horizon (Kwa et al., METR, 2025): measures autonomous capability as the length of tasks (in human-expert completion time) that a model completes with a given success probability, fitted by logistic regression of success vs. log human time over software/ML/cyber tasks (RE-Bench, HCAST, SWAA). TH1.1 (Jan 2026) uses 228 tasks and Inspect infrastructure. Unit: minutes (or hours) of human time; higher is better. arXiv:2503.14499; https://metr.org This id: 80% time horizon, TH1.1. https://metr.org/blog/2026-1-29-time-horizon-1-1/

benchmarks.name: Big Bench Audio
benchmarks.description: Big Bench Audio (Artificial Analysis, 2024): audio version of a subset of BIG-Bench Hard — 1,000 spoken questions from four reasoning categories (formal fallacies, navigate, object counting, web of lies), synthesized with 23 TTS voices; evaluates reasoning of speech-to-speech / audio-input models. Metric accuracy (%) graded by an LLM. License MIT. HF ArtificialAnalysis/big_bench_audio https://huggingface.co/datasets/ArtificialAnalysis/big_bench_audio

benchmarks.name: SuperGPQA
benchmarks.description: SuperGPQA (M-A-P / ByteDance Seed, 2025): graduate-level knowledge and reasoning benchmark of 26,529 multiple-choice questions (≈10 options) across 285 disciplines in 13 fields, annotated by 80+ experts with a human-LLM collaborative filtering pipeline. Metric accuracy (%). License ODC-BY. arXiv:2502.14739; HF m-a-p/SuperGPQA https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14739

benchmarks.name: Hrm8K
benchmarks.description: HRM8K (Ko, Son et al., HAE-RAE/OneLineAI, 2025): 8,011 English–Korean parallel bilingual math problems (GSM8K, MATH, Omni-MATH, MMMLU math plus Korean KSM competition problems) for measuring the multilingual math reasoning gap. Metric accuracy (%), usually averaged over subsets. arXiv:2501.02448 https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02448

benchmarks.name: FACTS Parametric
benchmarks.description: FACTS Parametric (Google DeepMind/Kaggle FACTS Leaderboard, 2025): sub-benchmark of the FACTS suite assessing world knowledge by answering closed-book factoid questions from internal parameters (no tools); public and private splits, graded by automated judges. Metric accuracy (%). arXiv:2512.10791; https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/google/facts https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10791

benchmarks.name: AGIEval
benchmarks.description: AGIEval (Zhong et al., Microsoft, 2023): human-centric benchmark built from official standardized exams — Gaokao (Chinese college entrance), SAT, LSAT, LSAT logic, math competitions (AMC/AIME), Chinese lawyer qualification and civil-service exams; 20 tasks / ~8,000 questions (English and Chinese), mostly multiple-choice. Metric accuracy (%). arXiv:2304.06364 https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06364

benchmarks.name: AA Mobile Intelligence (on-device avg)
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis Mobile Intelligence (2026): simple average of 5 evaluations representing on-device use — BFCL (subset), IFBench, AA-Omniscience, GPQA Diamond and MATH-500 — run on phone-sized (quantized) models with context limited to 16K tokens; score 0–100. https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/mobile-phone-intelligence-inference

benchmarks.name: AA Mobile End-to-End Generation Time
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis Mobile end-to-end generation time (2026, with Liquid AI): seconds for a model to process a 1,024-token prompt and generate a 256-token response on a reference phone (e.g. iPhone 17 Pro) with a given runtime/quantization; lower is better. https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/mobile-phone-intelligence-inference

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: composite 0–100 score from a weighted set of ~10 independently run evaluations (agentic work, coding, general knowledge/hallucination, long-context and scientific reasoning), pass@1, same harness for all models. Version 4.x launched early 2026 (current v4.3.2 components: AA-Briefcase, GDPval-AA, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, HLE, GDP.pdf, CritPt); scores across versions are not comparable. https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking This id: v4.0 index values.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.description: SWE-bench Verified (OpenAI Preparedness + SWE-bench team, Aug 2024): 500 human-validated tasks from the SWE-bench test set (real GitHub issues from 12 popular Python repos) screened by professional developers for well-specified issues and fair tests; the agent must produce a patch that makes the fail-to-pass unit tests pass without breaking others. Metric % resolved. HF princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified; base arXiv:2310.06770; https://www.swebench.com https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified

benchmarks.name: Open ASR Leaderboard English Avg WER
benchmarks.description: Open ASR Leaderboard (Srivastav et al., Hugging Face + partners, 2025): reproducible speech-recognition benchmark comparing open and proprietary systems across 12 datasets in English short-form (e.g. LibriSpeech, AMI, Earnings22, GigaSpeech, SPGISpeech, TED-LIUM, VoxPopuli), English long-form and multilingual tracks, with standardized text normalization. arXiv:2510.06961; https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard This id: average WER (%) over the English short-form datasets; lower is better. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06961

benchmarks.name: Open ASR Multilingual Avg WER
benchmarks.description: Open ASR Leaderboard (Srivastav et al., Hugging Face + partners, 2025): reproducible speech-recognition benchmark comparing open and proprietary systems across 12 datasets in English short-form (e.g. LibriSpeech, AMI, Earnings22, GigaSpeech, SPGISpeech, TED-LIUM, VoxPopuli), English long-form and multilingual tracks, with standardized text normalization. arXiv:2510.06961; https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard This id: average WER (%) on the multilingual track; lower is better. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06961

benchmarks.name: Open ASR Long-Form English Avg WER
benchmarks.description: Open ASR Leaderboard (Srivastav et al., Hugging Face + partners, 2025): reproducible speech-recognition benchmark comparing open and proprietary systems across 12 datasets in English short-form (e.g. LibriSpeech, AMI, Earnings22, GigaSpeech, SPGISpeech, TED-LIUM, VoxPopuli), English long-form and multilingual tracks, with standardized text normalization. arXiv:2510.06961; https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard This id: average WER (%) on the English long-form track; lower is better. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06961

benchmarks.name: Open ASR Leaderboard RTFx
benchmarks.description: Open ASR Leaderboard (Srivastav et al., Hugging Face + partners, 2025): reproducible speech-recognition benchmark comparing open and proprietary systems across 12 datasets in English short-form (e.g. LibriSpeech, AMI, Earnings22, GigaSpeech, SPGISpeech, TED-LIUM, VoxPopuli), English long-form and multilingual tracks, with standardized text normalization. arXiv:2510.06961; https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard This id: RTFx (inverse real-time factor = seconds of audio transcribed per second of compute on the reference GPU); higher is faster. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06961

benchmarks.name: Rtfx
benchmarks.description: RTFx (inverse real-time factor) for speech recognition: total audio duration divided by processing time (higher = faster), as standardized by the Open ASR Leaderboard (arXiv:2510.06961); value as reported by the source/hardware. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06961

benchmarks.name: AA STT Speed Factor (RTFx)
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis speech-to-text speed factor: seconds of audio transcribed per second of wall-clock time via the provider API (RTFx-style real-time factor; higher is faster). Definition follows the RTFx convention standardized by the Open ASR Leaderboard (arXiv:2510.06961). https://artificialanalysis.ai/speech-to-text

benchmarks.name: LibriSpeech test-clean WER
benchmarks.description: LibriSpeech (Panayotov, Chen, Povey, Khudanpur, ICASSP 2015): ~1,000 hours of 16 kHz read English audiobook speech from LibriVox; standard ASR test sets test-clean (5.4 h) and test-other (5.1 h, harder speakers). Metric word error rate (%), lower is better. License CC BY 4.0. https://www.openslr.org/12 This id: test-clean WER.

benchmarks.name: LibriSpeech test-other WER
benchmarks.description: LibriSpeech (Panayotov, Chen, Povey, Khudanpur, ICASSP 2015): ~1,000 hours of 16 kHz read English audiobook speech from LibriVox; standard ASR test sets test-clean (5.4 h) and test-other (5.1 h, harder speakers). Metric word error rate (%), lower is better. License CC BY 4.0. https://www.openslr.org/12 This id: test-other WER.

benchmarks.name: Toolathlon-Verified
benchmarks.description: Toolathlon (Tool Decathlon; Li et al., HKUST NLP, 2025): language-agent benchmark of 108 realistic, long-horizon tasks spanning 32 software apps and 604 tools via MCP servers (Google Calendar, Notion, WooCommerce, Kubernetes, BigQuery...), with realistic initial environment states and execution-based evaluators; ~20 tool-calling turns per task. arXiv:2510.25726; github.com/hkust-nlp/Toolathlon Toolathlon-Verified (June 2026): final verified release with reviewed prompts, ground truths and evaluators. benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (Verified)
benchmarks.description: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE): multimodal closed-ended academic benchmark at the frontier of human knowledge, built by CAIS and Scale AI with thousands of subject-matter experts (Phan et al., 2025). 2,500 expert-written questions (≈14% need an image) across dozens of subjects (math-heavy, plus humanities and natural sciences), multiple-choice and exact-match short-answer formats; each question has an unambiguous, non-searchable answer. Metric: accuracy (%), judged by an LLM answer-equality checker; calibration error also reported. Some boards (e.g. Artificial Analysis) use the 2,158-question text-only subset. arXiv:2501.14249; https://lastexam.ai Default setting: no tools.
